note: mapping_basis=data_labels. DERIVATION is core model s3 pattern 1: data/spain_2014_family.do infixes DA3032 at the ES3032 DATA LIST positions (P2501..P2504 = cols 229-232, identical to ES3032 line 21 and to the questionnaire's column codes (229)-(232)) under lower-cased names, and Bookmark 12 sets item = the variable name (p2501..p2504; lower-casing is Stata naming) -- nothing positional, so Step 5b is exempt and no verification_/verify_ files were written. LABELS vs QUESTIONNAIRE: ES3032 VARIABLE LABELS P2501-P2504 were compared with the P.25 rows of cues3032.pdf read from a 300-dpi render of scanned page 7 (not OCR), dot leaders dropped and the hyphenated line break 'obstácu-/lo' rejoined: 4/4 agree character for character (asserted in build.R), so item_text is both the label and the questionnaire row, with no override. Items are the four statements read out; item_text ships them as printed. VALUE LABELS identical on all 4: 1 'Muy de acuerdo' 2 'Bastante de acuerdo' 3 '(NO LEER) Ni de acuerdo ni en desacuerdo' 4 'Poco de acuerdo' 5 'Nada de acuerdo' 8 'N.S.' 9 'N.C.' -- matching the questionnaire's printed list (the scan renders the midpoint's 'ni' with a stray accent mark, 'ní'; immaterial, option 3 is not shipped). RESP BY DESIGN: the .do recodes 3 (the volunteered, not-read-out midpoint), 8 and 9 to missing, so live resp is {1,2,4,5} and option rows ship for those four codes only; there is no resp 3 row, and resp keeps its gap (4 = Poco de acuerdo, not the third option). Dropped by the .do, per item p2501..p2504: code 3 = 59/132/104/202 (497 total); code 8 = 30/43/31/37 (141); code 9 = 5/6/9/10 (30). DA3032 carries no code 0 and no blanks on cols 229-232, so P.25 was asked of all 2464 respondents (no filter printed above it); 49 respondents gave 3/8/9 on all four items and have no rows, which is why live has 2415 ids. CHECKED, decisive: reading DA3032 (2464 records, all 385 bytes; id = row number) at cols 229-232, dropping 3/8/9 as the .do does, with cov_sex col 254 and cov_age cols 255-256 (99 -> NA), reproduces the live table exactly: 9188 rows both, 2415 ids both, 0 only-live / 0 only-rebuilt rows, 0 resp, 0 cov_sex and 0 cov_age mismatches; cov_sex stored as the Stata value label (Hombre 4499 rows, Mujer 4689). Live item x resp (1/2/4/5): p2501 8/64/536/1762, p2502 70/298/520/1395, p2503 16/134/611/1559, p2504 288/797/406/724 -- every item uses all four levels; per-item n 2370/2283/2320/2215. Coherence: 'having children is an obstacle to a woman's professional life' (p2504, mean 3.2) is by far the most endorsed, the woman versions exceed the man versions for both marriage (4.3 vs 4.7) and children (3.2 vs 4.5), as the content predicts. validate_items.R --table-sets passed (4 items, resp {1,2,4,5}). TEXT (text_source=study_materials): instructions = the full P.25 question text verbatim from cues3032.pdf ('¿Está Ud. muy de acuerdo, bastante de acuerdo, poco o nada de acuerdo con estas frases?'), shared by all four rows, so instructions not section_prompt, one trivial section; the '(NO LEER)' marker belongs to the dropped option 3 and is not shipped. translation_source=machine_translation: CIS publishes Estudio 3032 in Spanish only; the _translated columns are English written by this project, option translations aligned with the siblings (Strongly agree / Quite agree / Slightly agree / Do not agree at all) -- issues-page line owed at upload. RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv CIS row (verdict allow, 2026-09-22, widened to every CIS survey year 2026-09-23, irw#2381) applied, not re-derived. DESCRIPTION: the IRW dictionary Description ('Agreement that marriage and having children are obstacles to the professional life of men and of women') names the four P.25 rows; no mismatch. Not confused with sibling _change (Bookmark 13, P.28). No response-data defect.
